intro.title: File storage systems
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a conceptual model of a basic file storage system to understand how files are organized, stored, and retrieved. You will learn the core concept of hierarchical directory structures, similar to folders on your computer, and how metadata like file names and sizes are managed. The main technologies involved are abstract data structures such as trees and key-value stores, which represent the system's organization and file attributes. By the end, you'll be able to design a simple system that can create directories, add files, and navigate through paths, giving you a foundational understanding of real-world storage solutions.
intro.usecase: File storage systems are foundational to countless applications, from cloud storage services like Dropbox and Google Drive to content management systems like WordPress and e-commerce platforms that handle product images. Developers implement these systems when building photo galleries in social media apps, document repositories in enterprise software, or media libraries in streaming services. Understanding file storage patterns is essential for creating efficient upload interfaces, organizing user-generated content, and ensuring reliable retrieval across distributed systems.
